instruction.text: Match the types of sentence to the examples.

atoms.a: Ben Nevis is the tallest mountain in UK.

feedback.end: A statement conveys a simple piece of information.

atoms.a: Bring the shopping in from the car before the ice cream melts.

feedback.end: A command contains a direct instruction telling someone to do something. They almost always have an imperative verb at the start of the main clause.

atoms.a: How many hours are you working today?

feedback.end: A question is used to gain further information from the person or people responding.
An exclamation expresses surprise, anger or any other intense feeling.

instruction.text: Choose the correct punctuation to end the different types of sentences.

atoms.b: The dog is playing with a tennis ball in the garden((++. ? ++!))

feedback.end: Statements usually end with a full stop, but they sometimes have an exclamation mark.

atoms.b: Put all the books back on the shelves before you leave((++. ? ++!))

feedback.end: Commands can either end with a full stop or an exclamation mark.

atoms.b: Would you like to go to a café to study today((. ++? !))

feedback.end: Questions must end with a question mark.

atoms.b: Wow, that was a very engaging meeting((. ? ++!))

feedback.end: Exclamations must end with an exclamation mark.
